This opportunity may also be remote.The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.PDI supports ARS researchers and stakeholders by providing technical assistance to develop, host, and maintain public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Services by PDI provide support to our scientists who are highly experienced in their research fields but may not have the technical, information technology (IT), or data science experience to build digital tools that optimize research efficiency and maximize the impact of their ARS research.Research Project: You will collaborate with the Partnerships for Data Innovations (PDI) team to train in the agile and innovative development of customized data solutions that promote collaboration and stewardship of ARS's research data and other knowledge assets. PDI is the only in-house public-facing enterprise-level data solutions provider for ARS scientists. Learning Objectives: You will learn a diversity of technical skillsets to develop, host, and maintain both internal and public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Specific training may include, but is not limited to, database development, web application development, and software development. You may request a remote training appointment.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Kyle Stoltz (kyle.stoltz@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: September 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of ARS and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: You will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. The anticipated stipend range is $6,617 - $6,680 monthly.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and ARS. Participants do not become employees of USDA, ARS, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.ARS.Plains@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.Qualifications The qualified candidate should be currently pursuing or have received an associate's or bachelor's degree in the one of the relevant fields. Preferred skills:Preferred educational background in computer sciences or related field.Any educational or work experience with agricultural data is a plus.Knowledge in computer programming (Python, HTML, Java, Powershell) and IT science/security experience also a plus.Stipend $6,617.00 – $6,680.00 MonthlyPoint of Contact JaneenEligibility Requirements Citizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Associate's Degree or Bachelor's Degree.

jobs.title: Policy Staff Summer Internship at Washington State Senate
jobs.description: Employer: Washington State Senate Expires: 08/29/2026 Policy Staff Summer InternshipWashington State Senate Republican Caucus The Washington State Senate Republican Caucus (SRC) is seeking a policy staff summer intern. The internship will commence in the spring or summer of 2027, after adjournment of the 2027 regular legislative session, and will run for eight weeks. Scheduling flexibility may be required depending on the needs of the Senate. The SRC is composed of 19 Washington state senators who serve together as a legislative caucus. The SRC is assisted by a staff of lawyers and analysts. The policy staff intern will work with SRC policy staff and will report to the SRC Leadership Counsel. The SRC policy staff internship is designed to provide opportunities for an enthusiastic law student to work with legislative lawyers in a caucus environment. The SRC policy staff internship will include specific assignments relating to legal research and bill drafting. The intern will also work with legislative staff to assist senators with committee meetings, task forces and work groups, constituent case work, and other similar activities. The SRC intends for the intern to gain exposure to legislators, lobbyists, state agency officials, and a variety of other professionals who work in and around the state legislature. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:The SRC is looking for a law student who is highly motivated to gain experience working on law and public policy matters in a legislative setting. SRC policy staff are “partisan staff,” and the caucus may consider whether the prospective intern’s approach to law and policy is an appropriate match. More information about the SRC can be found at src.wastateleg.org. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:The internship can be conducted either in-person on the Capitol campus in Olympia or remotely. The intern will be responsible for his or her own housing and transportation needs. SALARYThe SRC policy staff internship is not being offered for academic credit. The intern will be compensated at the rate of $3,821 per month. An intern will not receive additional employee benefits or paid time off. TO APPLY: Please submit the following by August 15, 2026.A letter of interestResumeLegal writing sampleUnofficial transcript Email your application materials to Saundra.richartz@leg.wa.gov Persons requiring reasonable accommodation in the application process or requiring information in an alternative format may contact the Senate Human Resource Office at Senate.HRO@leg.wa.gov. The Washington State Senate is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, creed, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, age, physical, sensory, or mental disability, honorably discharged veteran or military status, or the use of a service animal by a person with a disability.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: 2027 Corporate, Investment Banking and Markets (CIBM) Summer Intern Program - GCIB | New York at MUFG
jobs.description: Employer: MUFG Expires: 09/01/2026 On-the-Job Experience: Our 10-week Corporate, Investment Banking & Markets (CIB&M) Summer Intern Program is more than just a fascinating insight into MUFG: it is an opportunity to build the foundation for a long, rewarding career! Our program begins in early June and provides rising seniors with hands-on experience and business exposure in the world of global finance. We will place you with a specific group, which enables you to concentrate and quickly develop valuable skills and knowledge that are essential to becoming an integral part of the team. You will work alongside MUFG professionals at all levels who will serve as your instructors and mentors. Our summer interns will support deals and client-focused projects by conducting financial analysis, modeling and research, and assisting with pitch books and presentations. Our program is designed to help you grasp what it’s like to work within a global financial organization and decide where you want to take your career. Training: After one week of in-depth technical, financial products and/or markets training in New York, you will benefit from working alongside experienced colleagues on meaningful projects and will receive continuing on-the-job training throughout the 10-week program. Support & Guidance: Our team is committed to your success and will pair you with a mentor/manager who will work with you to set goals, provide professional development, guidance and conduct your performance review. You will also have many opportunities to network with peers, mentors and senior managers through team-building sessions, speakers and other organized events. In our open and inclusive environment, senior colleagues will know who you are and will see how your work impacts our high-performance culture. At the end of the program, you will leave with a better understanding of global banking/finance and an insider’s perspective that you'll only acquire from serving multinational clients with complex financial needs. Each summer intern gets a top-tier mentor in addition to their actual manager. The mentor will provide goals and professional development guidance and conduct performance reviews as a commitment to our summer interns. At the end of the program, you will obtain a better understanding of your group and how your role can play a part in the success of the bank.Business DivisionsCorporate Banking: Digital Infrastructure Investment Banking: Capital Markets, Global Financial Solutions, Project Finance

jobs.description: Employer: JPMorganChase Expires: 09/01/2026 About J.P. Morgan: J.P. Morgan is a leader in financial services, offering innovative and intelligent solutions to clients in more than 100 countries with one of the most comprehensive global product platforms available. jobs.title: 2027 Operations Analyst Program - Summer Analyst (NY Metro & Chicago) at JPMorganChase
jobs.description: Employer: JPMorganChase Expires: 09/01/2026 Be at the heart of running the firm efficiently, effectively, and delivering value for our clients. In the program, you will work in a collaborative environment that teaches you how the Operations function helps deliver core services to the firm and its clients. The goal is to assist you in building a long-term career in our Operations function and help with its continued growth. We are looking for motivated, enthusiastic individuals who want to begin and develop their career in Operations. We are looking for individuals with diverse backgrounds that are excited to learn and identify process opportunities (e.g., automation). As a Summer Analyst in the Operations Analyst Program, you will start our 9-week program with comprehensive training to introduce you to our firm, our practices, and our culture. After training, you will join the Operations function within one of our lines of business (Asset & Wealth Management, Commercial & Investment Bank, Consumer & Community Bank or Corporate Functions) to be fully ingrained within your team’s day-to-day activities and make a clear impact for the organization and our clients. You will make an impact in a specific Operations role aligned to our disciplines, which could include Processing/Servicing, Trade/Asset Support, Reporting, or Transformation. The program will give you the opportunity to learn about our operations and develop your career. Students interested in front office, external customer/client interactions, or software engineering will not have their needs met within this program.You will develop skills that will help you grow within the Operations organization and make increasing impact throughout the program. You will have the opportunity to expand your knowledge in businesses and bank products while driving our business forward. In addition to on-the-job experience, you will have a community of summer analysts, opportunity to attend social events, interaction with senior leaders, and more. This role is a pipeline to our full-time Operations Analyst Program; based on performance and successful completion of the 9-week internship, you may receive an offer of full-time employment.Your responsibilities will vary based on your assigned office location and role discipline. The responsibilities below align to each of our core role disciplines – Processing/Service, Trade/Asset, Reporting, and Transformation. Job responsibilities <Processing/Servicing>Assist with the end-to-end management of the client lifecycle, from onboarding through account maintenance. Partner with bankers, underwriters & various other functions to support client financing needs.Process, clear, investigate, and service transactions, tickets, and widgets responsibly. Support document review, data reconciliation, and payment processing. Reconcile differences between systems, monitoring reports and ensuring system integrity. <Trade/Asset Support>Analyze reference data to help support trading.Troubleshoot client inquiries related to account processing and access issues.Ensure the accurate execution of investor tickets and trades, following through to the correct settlement systems. Effectively communicate with counterparties to match off on trades.<Reporting>Support data analytics and reporting for your team and the lines of business you support, alongside other projects such as recertifications of heightened risk sector clients and creating processes that will minimize breaches in data input from the various lines of business.Oversee data management, governance, sourcing, control of reference data, and provide operational support.Report risk internally and externally, including running different attributions, investigating values, and presenting information to internal clients. <Transformation>Identify process gaps to optimize processes in collaboration with Technology teams. Create Tableau dashboards to assist in reporting.Implement AI and Machine Learning solutions into different Business Operations teams. Integrate products and information into easily accessible and digestible information for our internal clients. Required qualifications, capabilities, and skillsPursuing a B.A., B.S., B.B.A or 5th year M.A. or M.S., with an expected graduation date of December 2027 through June 2028All majors consideredWell-rounded academic background Great team player able to work and adapt in a dynamic and changing environmentDemonstrated ability to communicate effectively both written and verbally Detailed-oriented with strong critical thinking, attention to detail and analytical skillsAbility to manage time, prioritize assignments and know when to seek help for optimal solutionProficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook)Ability to work within deadlinesDemonstrated growth mindset with desire to learn financial operations Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skillsMinimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scaleLocations you can join:Chicago, ILNY Metro (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Jersey City) **Your exact office location maybe within proximity to one of our main hubs. jobs.description: Employer: Bain & Company Expires: 09/01/2026 At Bain, we want you to feel confident and supported as you consider what’s next—we know recruiting timelines aren’t one-size-fits-all. That’s why we are offering two application opportunities for our Associate Consultant Intern position in U.S. offices: March 29, 2026 and August 31, 2026.If you’re confident that consulting is your next step and are comfortable navigating earlier recruiting timelines, the Spring option may be right for you. If you’d prefer more time to explore firms, clarify your goals, and prepare for interviews, the Fall opportunity may be a better fit. We encourage you to apply when you’re ready and are happy to answer questions as you decide. Please refer to your school’s events calendar for opportunities to connect with recruiters and alumni.**********We invite current students to join our immersive internship. It'll offer broad exposure to the management consulting industry. You'll be staffed on one of our case teams and do real work interfacing with clients. If successful in the internship, it may lead to invitation for interviews or even an offer to join us as an associate consultant.This is a unique opportunity to work as an associate consultant at a top strategy consulting firm. It begins with one week of training after which point you’ll be staffed on a real case team where your background, opinion, and insights matter. You’ll own a distinct piece of that project and solve a challenging problem as a group. Unlike other programs, you’ll work directly on client cases. If you’re interested in understanding how businesses really make decisions, this is the place to find out.This program is typically for current bachelor’s and master’s students with one full summer left before graduation. The exact deadlines may vary by region—check our office information for exact details.The following are typical requirements to apply for the Associate Consultant Internship. Additionally, in some locations compensation may vary based on several factors including, but not limited to relevant experience, education, licensure/certifications, training and skill level.Compensation for this role in the United States includes a monthly base salary of $9,000 and Bain’s best-in-class benefits package (details listed below).Bain & Company's comprehensive U.S. benefits and wellness program is designed to help employees achieve personal independence, protection and stability in the areas most important to you and your family. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Urban Agriculture Intern at Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
jobs.description: Employer: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens Expires: 09/02/2026 POSITION DESCRIPTION Urban Agriculture Intern Vizcaya Museum and Gardens is a National Historic Landmark and accredited museum in Miami, Florida (www.vizcaya.org). The Urban Agriculture Intern is a hands‑on position that helps connect Vizcaya’s growing spaces with its public and educational programs during the peak agricultural season. Working across cultivation, harvest support, and seasonal program preparation, the role contributes to how crops are grown, interpreted, and shared with visitors. The position is on the Engagement & Cultural Resources Team in the Horticulture & Sustainability Department and reports to the Senior Horticulturist and Horticulture Manager. The role is ideal for emerging professionals interested in food systems, agriculture, and sustainability. Vizcaya is owned by Miami‑Dade County and operated by the Vizcaya Museum and Gardens Trust, Inc. Our mission is to preserve the estate’s cultural and environmental resources to engage people in connecting with the past, understanding the present, and shaping the future. Our vision is a “Home for Miami, an Inspiration for All.” Essential Functions• Conduct routine data collection across growing areas, documenting operations, crop performance, harvests, and seasonal field conditions.• Support plant propagation, crop care, harvesting, and post-harvest processing, including documenting yields and plant development.• Use landscape hand tools, power equipment, and post-harvest tools safely and effectively.• Assist with volunteer coordination, nursery management, and general plant care tasks.• Track crop schedules, harvest timing, seasonal growing patterns, and field observations through consistent recordkeeping.• Help identify and document edible crops suited to South Florida conditions and diversified planting strategies.• Support educational and public programming by tracking crop availability and maintaining records aligned with tours, workshops, and Farmers Market demonstrations. This internship description is not designed to be comprehensive; duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. Learning OpportunitiesThis intern will gain:Hands‑on skills with food‑processing equipment.Skills in post‑harvest handling and product preparation. Experience taking field notes that are detailed, structured records of observations, activities, and decisions made on a farm.An understanding of how crop cycles connect to educational experiences, including K–8 school tours and adult workshops. Position RequirementsHigh school diploma or equivalent with an interest in urban agriculture, food systems, sustainability, or environmental work.Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions and safely traverse uneven surfaces.Ability to lift and carry up to 40 lbs.Strong communication skills, attention to detail, and ability to maintain clear, organized records.Ability to work independently and collaboratively.Comfort with documenting observations, maintaining consistent field notes, and supporting basic agricultural recordkeeping is required.English fluency CompensationThe salary for this internship is $20/hour. Work Environment/Physical DemandsThe majority of work takes place outdoors in Vizcaya’s agricultural growing spaces, including The Field, perennial and annual beds, and nearby program areas—often in South Florida heat, humidity, and variable weather conditions. Tasks require standing, kneeling, bending, lifting up to 40 lbs, and performing repetitive motions during planting, harvesting, and maintenance. Some work will occur indoors in programming or processing areas (such as Teaching Kitchen prep spaces or storage rooms) when preparing educational materials or assisting with equipment. Vizcaya is a non‑smoking environment. Position Type/Expected Hours of Work/ScheduleThis is a part-time internship averaging 24 hours per week for 50 consecutive weeks, beginning on a rolling basis in the fall and aligned with Vizcaya’s primary growing seasons. The intern will work three days per week, Monday through Friday, with occasional weekend shifts as needed. Daily hours will vary based on field operations, program activities, and seasonal priorities. To Apply Please submit a resume and a cover letter expressing your interest in this position to: https://vizcaya.org/about/careers/. Equal Opportunity EmployerVizcaya Museum and Gardens is committed to equity and inclusion and is engaged in a strategic process to ensure that our staff, Board, and volunteers reflect our community’s diversity. Vizcaya welcomes applicants from groups that are underrepresented in cultural organizations and seeks to recruit, develop and retain a diverse workforce. Vizcaya Museum and Gardens is an equal opportunity employer. Vizcaya respects people of all backgrounds and does not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, pregnancy, childbirth, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, familial status, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, status as a victim of domestic violence, dating violence or stalking, or other applicable legally protected characteristics protected by law. jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/03/2026 Marketing Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the marketing team and touches everything: what we publish, what we spend, and whether the growth engine actually compounds. Read the whole post before applying.This is not make-a-mood-board-and-watch. You'll be publishing real content under our name, running real campaigns with real budgets behind them, and owning numbers that leadership actually looks at. Real deadlines, real consequences, with the Marketing Manager beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the marketing engine actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doContent and channelsWrite across everything we publish: blog posts, emails, landing pages, social content, campaign copy. What you write goes live.Support SEO research, format and optimize blog content, and build and maintain website pages.Schedule and publish across our social channels, then track what performs and say why.Engage physician conversations across forums, social platforms, and the communities where our audience already spends time. You'll be speaking as the firm, so precision matters.Build graphics and marketing assets to support campaigns across channels.Campaigns and operationsEmail: build and proof campaigns before they go out, manage list segmentation, and catch the typo before ten thousand physicians see it.Paid media: support campaign assets, pull performance data, and track results against goals.Partnerships: track deliverables across partner programs and keep co-branded content moving. Nobody chases you; you chase them.Events and webinars: promotional assets, registration pages, post-event follow-up.Analytics: keep tracking and attribution clean, build regular performance reports, and dig into what's working and what isn't. When a number looks wrong, find out why before someone asks.Research: track competitors and market trends, and surface what's worth acting on.Growth projects: help launch channels and platforms we don't have yet.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Writing. You write clean, tight copy that doesn't need a rewrite before it ships. You know the difference between words that fill space and words that move someone. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Detail. Marketing looks polished or sloppy based entirely on the small things: the broken link, the wrong UTM, the subject line that renders badly on mobile. You catch these before they go out, not after.Numbers and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A campaign's attribution is off, a partner deliverable is nine days late, two reports disagree on last month's leads. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is scheduling, formatting, data cleanup, and tracking spreadsheets. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real brand or spend exposure (budget decisions, public statements on tax positions, partner commitments) is yours to prepare and the Marketing Manager's to decide. You will never be left holding that alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.A flexible schedule built around your classes.RequirementsPursuing a degree in marketing or a related program.Strong written communication. Be ready to prove it.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new tools and platforms quickly.Familiar with marketing channels and how they connect to each other.Curious about a niche industry. Physician tax is more interesting than it sounds.Prior marketing experience is a plus: an internship, a class project, a club, or something you built yourself.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.description: Employer: American Institute of Physics Expires: 09/03/2026 POSITION TITLE: Science Writer, Intern WHO WE ARE: As a Federation, AIP advances the success of a community of more than 30 independent scientific organizations. They, in turn, support hundreds of thousands of professionals across many scientific and engineering disciplines. AIP creates shared spaces — forums, conversations, connections — where individual action among our Member Organizations becomes collective impact. You'll also gain valuable experience collaborating with editors, researchers, and communications professionals while building a strong portfolio of published work. Demonstrated interest in science, research, and science communication. Ability to research complex topics and communicate them clearly to broad audiences. Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Ability to collaborate effectively with a team while working independently on assigned projects. Experience in journalism, communications, or science writing is preferred but not required. TO APPLY: Include a resume and a cover letter. We encourage you to apply even if your experience does not fully match the position description. At AIP, we embrace considering people from a diversity of backgrounds and career experiences. COMPENSATION: $18.80 - $19.20 per hour WORKING AT AIP: AIP embraces a flexible hybrid work environment to balance in-person collaborative work with remote work. The team works in a flexible, hybrid schedule and reports to our offices in College Park, Maryland and Washington, DC, as needed. Employees are required to reside in the DC Metro regions of Maryland, Virginia, or Washington, DC. Your colleagues at AIP are welcoming, gracious, and eager to help each other succeed. With our commitment to community service, institute-wide social opportunities, and ongoing learning and development, AIP is a rewarding place to work. ABOUT AIP: Scientific discovery shapes our lives every day. And AIP empowers the organizations and people that make those discoveries possible.As a Federation, AIP advances the success of a community of more than 30 independent scientific organizations. They, in turn, support hundreds of thousands of professionals across many scientific and engineering disciplines. AIP creates shared spaces — forums, conversations, connections — where individual action among our Member Organizations becomes collective impact.As an Institute, AIP preserves the history of discovery so the past can guide the future. We study how research is done, who participates, and what holds people back or propels them to succeed. Our findings inform policy, practice, and decision-making across the physical sciences. We are especially focused on the next generation of physical scientists and committed to ensuring talent from anywhere can thrive in our fields. Humanity needs science. And science needs people and organizations working together to tackle our planet’s toughest challenges. Together, we can advance science, empower scientists, and ensure discovery continues to shape our lives. jobs.title: Operations Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/03/2026 Operations Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This internship is how we find the people who run our operations for the long haul. Read the whole post before applying.This is not coffee-and-shadowing. You'll be in the middle of how the firm actually runs: talking to real physician clients, moving them through onboarding, keeping our boards clean, and making sure entity and vendor orders get placed and land. Real deadlines that matter to real businesses, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the machine works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doClient follow-up. Chase down what we need, answer what you can, keep clients moving. You'll be writing to physicians directly, so the writing has to be clean.Client onboarding. Run new clients through our process end to end and make sure nothing falls through.Monday boards. Keep them accurate and current. Statuses, owners, dates, subitems. If the board is wrong, the firm is flying blind.Data management and cleanup. Fixing records, reconciling lists, catching what doesn't match. Some of this is genuinely tedious. It still has to be right.Entity orders with vendors. Place them, track them, follow up until the documents are in hand.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And you have to be honest with yourself about the manual work. Not every task here is interesting. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsPursuing a degree in accounting, finance, business, math, or a related program.Strong written communication. Comfortable with numbers and spreadsheets.Tolerance for repetitive work when the repetition is what makes the output correct.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.title: Finance Development Program Intern at Michigan Medicine - Finance Development Program
jobs.description: Employer: Michigan Medicine - Finance Development Program Expires: 09/03/2026 Program Overview The Finance Development Program (FDP) hires undergraduate juniors with an interest in finance, strategy, and healthcare to complete a summer internship. The project-based program offers an enriching summer experience involving several areas of Michigan Medicine, with the goal of enhancing financial abilities, leadership acumen, and knowledge of the business side of healthcare. Top-performing interns are eligible for offers to join the full-time, rotation-based, two-year program the following summer. The goal of the full-time program is to offer increased development of the skills and experiences needed by analysts to accelerate and advance their careers at Michigan Medicine through in-depth, six-month projects throughout the organization. Position Description Over the summer, candidates will work on several project-based assignments spanning a wide range of Michigan Medicine operations and skills sets. As an analyst, candidates will gain exposure across areas including financial governance, departmental analysis functions, and assisting with senior leadership responsibilities. Rotational opportunities include, but are not limited to: Clinical Financial Planning and Analysis Enterprise Financial Reporting and Forecasting Financial Systems Medical School Finance Reimbursement Strategic Finance and Business Consulting Upon completion of the program, analysts will have developed their finance and leadership skills alongside extensive industry knowledge. Improvement and learning will be showcased through a work portfolio developed over the course of the program. FDP projects often require the collaboration of different functional teams, giving program members a unique perspective, and a better understanding of how Michigan Medicine operates. Additionally, some projects allow for engagement with external stakeholders, including insurers, government entities, and strategic partners. Qualifications Ideal candidates meet the following qualifications: Completing junior year of a Bachelor’s program in Finance, Accounting, Business, Healthcare Administration, Economics, Statistics, Math, or a related field. Candidates from other disciplines with a keen interest in finance and/or healthcare are also welcome to apply. Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities. Strong analytical skills with a meticulous attention to detail. Ability to thrive in a dynamic work environment and manage evolving projects effectively. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Tableau, financial intelligence software, and basic relational database management. A cover letter is required for consideration for this position. The cover letter should address your specific interest in the position and outline skills that directly relate to the role. Additional Information The mission of Michigan Medicine is to improve the health of patients, populations, and communities through excellence in education, patient care, community service, research, and technology development, and through leadership activities in Michigan, nationally and internationally. With annual revenues of approximately $8 billion, Michigan Medicine ranks as one of the top academic health centers in the country, and is committed to providing exceptional patient care, facilitating groundbreaking research and developing the next generation of physicians and scientists. Michigan Medicine consists of the Hospitals, Health Centers and Clinics, the University of Michigan Medical School and its Medical Group, and the Michigan Health Corporation. Michigan Medicine conducts background screening and pre-employment drug testing on job candidates upon acceptance of a contingent job offer and may use a third party administrator to conduct background screenings. Background screenings are performed in compliance with the Fair Credit Report Act. *Please note this internship is for undergraduate students only* *Applicants can expect to hear about next steps after the application deadline* For more information please visit: Finance Development Program (umich.edu)

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: HR Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/03/2026 HR Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits next to the COO and touches everything: who we hire, how they get onboarded, and whether the firm's people operations actually run. Read the whole post before applying.This is not coffee-and-shadowing. You'll be in the COO's calendar and inbox, running real recruiting pipelines, onboarding real employees across a fully remote firm operating in all 50 states, and holding the follow-up loop on things senior people delegated and then moved on from. Real deadlines, real consequences, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the firm actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doExecutive support to the COOOwn the calendar. Schedule, reschedule, protect deep-work blocks, resolve conflicts across pods.Triage the inbox. Sort it, flag what needs a decision, draft replies for approval, clear the routine yourself.Prep every recurring meeting: agenda, prior action items, the two or three numbers needed to run it.Capture action items out of leadership and pod meetings and chase them until they close, including with people more senior than you.Turn dictated voice notes into structured documents, specs, and task lists.Travel, expenses, receipts, card reconciliation, and document organization in Drive.Gatekeep and route inbound asks so the COO sees decisions, not queues.People operationsRecruiting. Source and post roles, screen inbound applicants against our rubrics, schedule interviews, keep the Monday recruiting board clean, run first-round screening calls from a guide, and make sure no candidate is left hanging.Onboarding. Own the pre-start checklist end to end: system provisioning, equipment shipping, I-9, state new-hire reporting, W-4 and state withholding forms, handbook and policy sign-offs, day one and 30/60/90 plans.Offboarding. Exit checklist, same-day access revocation, equipment recovery, benefits notices.Multi-state compliance support. Help maintain our 50-state employment requirements matrix, new state registrations with payroll, PTO and sick leave rules, poster distribution, and flag legislative changes that actually hit us.Payroll and benefits admin support in Gusto: data hygiene, time off tracking, open enrollment logistics, verification letters.Credentials tracking. PTIN renewals, CPA and EA license calendars, CPE hours by person.Documentation. Job descriptions, org chart, HR SOPs, handbook upkeep, internal knowledge base.Performance and review cycle logistics: reminders, completion tracking, data prep. Logistics and prep, not decisions.Culture and engagement: offsite project management, surveys, milestones, welcome announcements.People data. Headcount and attrition reporting, and cleanup across Gusto, Monday, and Workspace.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Communication. You write clean, professional messages to candidates, employees, vendors, and outside counsel without them needing a rewrite. You follow up without being asked. You don't go quiet when something is stuck.Judgment and discretion. You'll see comp, performance conversations, and personnel files. That information does not leave your hands. You'll also learn quickly what the COO needs to decide versus what you should just handle.Logic and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A new hire's state paperwork is missing, a candidate has been sitting in stage two for nine days, two systems disagree on someone's title. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is checklists, forms, data cleanup, and scheduling. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real legal exposure (classification calls, workplace investigations, terminations, comp decisions) is yours to prepare and the COO's to decide. You will never be left holding that alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsPursuing a degree in human resources, business, accounting, communications, or a related program.Strong written communication. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new software quickly.Discretion with confidential information, without needing to be reminded.Tolerance for repetitive work when the repetition is what makes the output correct.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.title: Culinary Internship: Meat and Dairy at Deck Family Farm
jobs.description: Employer: Deck Family Farm Expires: 09/03/2026 This is perfect for someone who is interested in the culinary side of farming! We’re looking for someone passionate about creating high-quality food and cares about how those animals were raised. Some of the key things you will learn are: Animal butchery, sausage making, cheesemaking, rendering lard, making broth, knife, kitchen, and cooking skills, spreadsheeting, and record keeping.You will be an important part of our house-made, value-added products program. You will primarily work alongside our processing manager and be trained through hands-on experience with written Standard Operating Procedures. This is a very dynamic role. A usual week will consist of producing and packaging 1-2 batches of value-added meat product (sausage, broth, lard, or pet food) and 1-2 batches of cheese/week. There are also semi-annual events and dinners that happen here, so you will assist in preparing those meals. April-November is poultry processing season so you will be part of the crew processing chickens and turkeys from live animal to packaged product. When needed, animals need to be put down due to disability or sickness. When possible, we save this meat for ourselves or our farm dogs. This is an opportunity to learn how to humanely and respectfully kill and process livestock.You will also assist in delivering our livestock to our USDA processor and picking up the resulting packaged product. This is a very important part of running the farm that takes an often-overlooked degree of knowledge and planning. These are integral skills and protocols to know, especially if you intend on raising animals for slaughter and sale in the future.This program will prepare you for work in many food handling and preparation jobs. It will be a great way to learn butchery skills if you have goals of becoming a butcher, meat processor, homesteader, chef, or own a livestock farm. There are also many opportunities for working on the farm and gaining animal husbandry experience. About 30 hours/week are dedicated to meat and dairy processing. The remaining 20 hours can be made up in our other intern tracks that are listed above. If you are interested in this companion program, the best contact is Jeremy at 716-410-2933 or Deckfamilyfarm@gmail.com.The Farm:Deck Family Farm is located in Western Willamette Valley. The farm is a highly diversified operation that focuses on Regenerative Agriculture practices using pasture based animal systems. Own and lease approximately 300-500 acres. Animal groups include Heritage Red Wattle Pork, Heritage Galloway Beef, Pastured Poultry, Lamb, Jersey Dairy Cows and Organic Layer Hens. Products include beef, pork, lamb, chicken, raw milk, milk products & artisan cheese, organic eggs, fruit, nuts, and vegetable market garden. Deck Family farm stands on the principle of sustainability in all forms; energetic, environmental, and financial. Practices currently employed include riparian exclusion and restoration, managed intensive grazing, humane animal handling, reforestation and oak woodland planting, nutrient management, ethical business practice, transparency and traditional family values. The farm practices regenerative agriculture improving soil through nutrient management systems of assessing soil needs, applying composted manures, ash, and lime. DFF employs a 7-year rotation to graze, renovate and restore pastures. Over the last 20 years the farm has put 1 mile plus of riparian corridors into the Creek Restoration & Enhancement Program (CREP), performed 5 Environment Quality Incentive Program (EQUIP) projects to sequester and compost manure on farm, and planted over 100,000 trees through the Forest Trust Program. All forage produced on farm is certified organic with Oregon Tilth. Deck Family Farm maintains a humane handling certification with GAP (Good Animal Practices), is AGA (American Grass-fed Association) Certified, and holds Salmon Safe certification for our creek and riparian restoration work. Deck strives to build reasonable efficiencies and economies of scale for financial resiliency while acknowledging that the lives of the animals we raise and the people we feed are all sacred. DFF runs a year-round education program for 8-10 intern/trainees and apprentices that includes a cost of living allowance, introduces trainees to neighboring farms, supports externships and on and off farm research projects. Approximately 50% of DFF graduates continue into some sector of the agriculture industry. The workday begins at 7 AM with an all farm meeting, milking, and farm chores. We break for an hour at noon and finish the day between 4 to 6PM. The work week is 5 days on 2 days off, 8-10 hours/day. We appreciate flexibility depending on the season and work load.Accommodations are modest, either shared housing in an intern room, cabin or COB (Adobe) house.Deck Family Farm is a multi-generational and community-oriented farm. The ideal applicant thrives in a full and rich environment of activity and diversity. The farm has an open gate; policy that welcomes visitors any day but Sunday. Deck is dedicated to being transparent in our practice and is committed to keeping our agricultural heritage alive and relevant for our farm community and beyond.In order to apply, please contact Jeremy Hyland: 716-410-2933 or Deckfamilyfarm@gmail.comMore information about the farm: www.DeckFamilyFarm.com

jobs.title: Social Media Intern at Meyocks
jobs.description: Employer: Meyocks Expires: 09/05/2026 Everyone else offers internships. But we’re not like everyone else. And neither are you. At Meyocks, we believe getting real world experience in this industry is ultimately going to mean more for you than just making coffee runs. That’s why we don’t offer internships here. We offer mentorships. And our mentorships are for those who are just as serious about this industry as they are about making a mark in it. Meyocks is searching for a Social Media Intern ready to jump headfirst into agency life. You’ll work closely with our social media, public relations, and content teams supporting social while also collaborating with creative directors and art directors to help brands mean more. This is an excellent opportunity for someone interested in learning the fundamentals of social media within a fast-paced, collaborative agency environment. Job Summary:The Social Media intern will support the Meyocks team in assisting with the creation, scheduling, and management of content across multiple platforms, including Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and client websites. This intern will assist with content ideation, light video editing, community management, and basic social media performance reporting while gaining hands-on experience with brand, social media and analytics. Key ResponsibilitiesAssisting with ideating and creating social media content that aligns with brand voice and platform best practicesSupporting scheduling, publishing, and community management across platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and FacebookMonitoring comments, direct messages, and mentions across social channelsHelping compile basic monthly or quarterly analytics and performance insightsMonitoring social media channels for brand mentions, conversations, and emerging trends, providing insights to help inform content strategy and community engagementIdentifying trending audio, hashtags, and content formats that align with the brandsBrainstorming creative content ideas for campaigns, seasonal moments, and trending topicsStaying informed on platform updates and emerging social media features Required Skills/Abilities:Familiarity with major social media platforms and interest in content creation (photo, video, short-form)Basic experience with light video editing and design tools (e.g., CapCut, Canva, iMovie, or similar)Strong communication skills, attention to detail, and eagerness to learn social media and analyticsAbility to organize information clearly and manage multiple tasks in a deadline-driven environment Education and Experience:A student working towards a bachelor's degree in advertising, communications, public relations, marketing or related fields.Experience in Microsoft Office and project management software such as Asana.1-2 years of relevant experience through internships, campus activities, volunteering, class work or transferable work experience. Other Requirements:Internship can be virtual, in-person or hybrid.Looking for part-time fall intern.Meyocks can be flexible with hours.
